bull.b: GSK’s candidate selection provides external validation of Wave’s proprietary chemistry and SpiNA design capabilities. Continued platform productivity across RNAi, RNA editing and related modalities could support multiple programs and create additional partnering opportunities over the next several quarters.

FDA alignment on a potentially streamlined WVE-006 registration strategy could reduce development complexity and shorten the route to approval if clinical results support the plan. The program also targets both lung and liver manifestations of AATD, strengthening its potential differentiation.

The projected cash runway into the third quarter of 2028 gives Wave time to advance several clinical programs without an immediate financing requirement. This supports sustained investment in WVE-006, WVE-007 and WVE-008 while allowing future milestones to provide additional funding optionality.

bear.b: Heavy recurring cash consumption indicates that Wave has not yet achieved operating leverage and must continue funding substantial research and development spending. If losses persist, future capital raises or collaboration proceeds may remain important to sustain the expanding clinical portfolio.

WVE-007’s investment case still depends on forthcoming evidence that its early body-composition and tolerability profile translates into meaningful, durable weight loss. Pending dose, efficacy and safety data leave clinical differentiation and eventual regulatory success unresolved.

Unfinalized pivotal endpoints and dosing create execution risk for WVE-006 even after favorable FDA discussions. Additional decisions on clinical measurements, regimen and exposure could affect trial design, timelines, enrollment demands and the probability of achieving a commercially useful label.
